# Subsetting {.hero #s00g-subsetting}

::: {.section-badge}
Basics · `[`, `[[`, and `$`
:::

## On data frames and tibbles

```{webr-r}
df1 <- data.frame(x = 1:3,
                  y = c("a", "b", "c"),
                  z = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE))

# a whole column (still a data frame)
df1[1]

# rows × columns
df1[1, 1:2]

# a column as a vector (unwrapped)
df1$x

# the 3rd element of that vector
df1$x[3]
```

`df[i]` keeps the data-frame wrapper; `df$x` gives you the raw vector.

## On lists

```{webr-r}
list_a <- list(x = 1:3,
               y = c("a", "b", "c"))

# 1st element — still a list of length 1
list_a[1]

# 1st element unwrapped — the vector inside
list_a[[1]]

# then index into that vector
list_a[[1]][1]
```

**Rule of thumb:** single brackets `[ ]` preserve the container type; double brackets `[[ ]]` and `$` extract the contents.
